names: Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall
summary: A ~165,000 sq ft, five-story research building at 1550 4th St housing UCSF's human genetics, developmental biology and neuroscience programs and the Center for Brain Development, notable for early use of Japanese seismic-isolation technology.

milestones.text: UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings certifies a CEQA EIR addendum and approves the design of the Mission Bay Developmental Biology and Genetics Building (Building 19B) -- believed to be this building based on matching architect (Cesar Pelli and Associates with Flad Associates as executive architect), size (~171,000 gsf) and programs (human genetics, developmental neuroscience, developmental biology), though the Regents item does not use the 'Rock Hall' name; an $88,000,000 total project budget was approved in March 2000, with construction slated for 2001-2003
Rock Hall opens (opening year is contested across sources: 2002, 2004 and one secondary '2005' reference; 2004 is the best-supported reading)

costs.what: Total project budget the UC Regents approved in March 2000 for the Mission Bay Developmental Biology and Genetics Building (Building 19B) -- believed to be this building based on matching architect, size and programs, per the May 2000 Regents design-approval item that recounts the budget action; neither item uses the 'Rock Hall' name

facts.value: Pelli Clarke Pelli Architects (Cesar Pelli) with Flad Architects

open_questions: Opening year is genuinely contested: some project/engineering pages cite 2002 (likely confused with groundbreaking), UCSF's own historical archive and a 2005 design-award mention support 2004, and one secondary summary says 2005. Recorded as 2004, flagged approximate, not resolved further.
Exact opening month not found in any source checked.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

This building's photo (from a Sept. 2008 Regents presentation) has no independently confirmed capture date; it predates or coincides with that presentation, which is well after the building's own completion date, so it's tagged 'now' as the only photograph found rather than 'completed'. No site plan or rendering specific to this building was found in a public-record source.

2026-09-21 pass: identified a strong but not certain candidate for this building's design-approval milestone -- a May 2000 Regents item for the 'Mission Bay Developmental Biology and Genetics Building (19B).' The match rests on architect, square footage, program and block-adjacency (19B sits next to the later Sandler Neurosciences Center on Block 19A, consistent with Rock Hall's known position), but the Regents item itself never uses the name 'Rock Hall' -- a donor-naming gift presumably came later. Not fully closed.
